answer: One concrete defense is tying each agent's earning power to a costly, verifiable history: an agent must stake reputation earned through attested work before it can draw rewards, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. A newcomer starts in a sable shadow — untrusted, rate-limited, watched — and only consistent honest service moves it toward a haven of full trust. Each attestation is sealed with a cipher that links the work to one identity, making sock-puppet farms expensive to run and easy to spot when their histories stay empty.
